title: He Makes $4K/Day With This Weird Middleman Business
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The guest is promoting his own cake-gifting company and asks viewers to contact him on LinkedIn or Instagram to buy cakes. The host plugs his paid community Playmakers.ai.com for AI consultants and agencies. Some numbers conflict: the business is called 'six weeks' old in one place and '1.5 months' after the pivot in another. The guest says 'we're cooked' and must fundraise, then says 'We're profitable right now'. Profit is given as both 40k and '30, 40 grand'.

stated_problem.quote: So in a world like that, we're not going to be able to send cold emails, we're not going to be able to send LinkedIn DMs or cold calling one 'cause there's gonna be too much noise.
stated_problem.speaker: William Lindholm

idea.name: Cold-caking outbound gifting service
idea.one_liner: A managed service plus software that sends premium cakes from local partner bakeries to a B2B company's prospects (or existing customers) to book sales meetings. It charges about $50-70 per cake and keeps the margin over a discounted bakery price.
idea.customer: B2B sales teams, mainly software and SaaS companies, plus accountants, real estate brokers and agencies with a high contract value
idea.offer: Sourcing, ordering and tracking cake deliveries at scale (bulk recipient upload, delivery photos, order tracking), email-then-cake-then-follow-up sequences, and 'retention cakes' for existing customers
idea.revenue_model: Per-cake price (about $50-70 at volume) minus a discounted bakery cost, giving roughly 30% gross profit ($30-40k on $120k/month). Possible recurring batches via CRM integration and territory revenue-share or franchise deals

I mean, we put software on top of it to make logistics better.
And then we let them track all the orders, all the different bakeries are taking pictures per delivery and so on.
If we can become the company that has the most data on what kind of gifts work, we become the next Apollo or the next like real big GTM engine.
it becomes this marketing loop because if you send a cake to X company, then X

Maybe I go like, "Hey, we have this brand and you can have this area and we'll take a split revenue.

acquisition_channels.details: Stunts that went viral, such as a pitch-deck cake sent to VCs (posted on X) and a unicorn cake, which led to tech news coverage and inbound leads. Recipients post cakes on social media, which brings in more inbound.
People who received a cake and booked a meeting then ask to use the service themselves (a 'marketing loop').
A sequence: an email saying a cake arrives in two days and asking to confirm the address, then the cake, then a follow-up by email or phone.
Cold-caked VC firms (a16z, Sequoia) as a PR stunt. The guest invites buyers to contact him on LinkedIn or Instagram.

ideas.delivery: Local partner patisseries, sourced and negotiated with by an AI agent, bake and deliver the cakes and photograph each delivery. The company's software handles bulk recipient upload and order tracking. Cakes are occasionally flown to niche locations. The founder and a small team handle fulfilment and are currently overloaded.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Outreach to prospects is B2B cold email, which PECR allows to limited companies if an opt-out is offered; sole-trader prospects would need consent. Sending physical gifts by post or courier is outside PECR's electronic rules, but recipient names and addresses are personal data under UK GDPR (legitimate interests assessment, data processing agreements with clients). Bakery partners must follow food hygiene and allergen information rules. The Bribery Act 2010 means gift values should stay modest, especially for public-sector recipients.

idea.name: Automated employee birthday cakes
idea.one_liner: Software that connects to a company's HR or payroll system and automatically sends a bakery cake on employees' birthdays or milestone birthdays. The company pays per cake on a recurring basis.
idea.customer: Employers (e.g. a 40-employee company) in markets with a culture of employee recognition, such as Norway
idea.offer: Employee birthdays are pulled from HR systems and cakes are delivered automatically, so nobody gets forgotten
idea.revenue_model: Recurring per-cake invoicing (about $80 per cake, roughly 50% margin), with high retention and low churn

acquisition_channels.details: In Norway, outbound cold calls offering a free cake for a meeting. It worked well there; it was never tried in the US.
About 40 US ads A/B tested with zero conversions

ideas.delivery: Integrations with about 40 HR and payroll systems (e.g. Gusto, ADP, Paychex) trigger orders, and local bakeries deliver the cakes. The guest's mother handles customer service.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Employee birthdates taken from HR systems are personal data under UK GDPR, so a data processing agreement with each employer is required. Cold calls to businesses must be screened against CTPS. Auto-renewing subscriptions may fall under DMCC Act subscription rules if any customers are consumers or sole traders.

idea.name: AI-agent supplier sourcing and negotiation network
idea.one_liner: An AI agent that runs every two hours to find local suppliers (bakeries), email them a bulk-order offer, and negotiate discounts, escalating deals to the founder for a thumbs up or down. It builds a fulfilment network that could be reused for other product categories.
idea.customer: Internal capability for a fulfilment marketplace (the guest says it could extend beyond cakes)
idea.offer: An automatically built network of local suppliers with negotiated discounts
idea.revenue_model: Margin on fulfilment from discounted supplier pricing (about 30% discount)

key_quotes.quote: So the way I do it now is I have like this super prompt in cloud core work, connected to a superhuman MCP, super human is like an email system.
If the discount is good enough, my agent sends that email to my personal email where I just give a thumbs up or a thumbs down on it.
And I can take that and do that with so much more than just cakes and bakeries.
We only partner with like organic, French, Patisserie's, make quality cakes

acquisition_channels.details: The AI agent cold-emails bakeries (as suppliers) with a bulk purchase offer, then negotiates a discount and cites Forbes coverage

ideas.delivery: The Claude Cowork agent with a 'super prompt' and Superhuman email MCP runs every two hours. It finds bakeries (checking reviews), emails them, and negotiates. The founder approves or rejects deals by thumbs up or down.

uk_legal_risk.reason: Not flagged: these emails are purchase or procurement enquiries to suppliers, not marketing, so PECR's marketing rules are unlikely to apply. Wording that pitches a partnership programme to sole-trader bakeries could still count as marketing.

ideas.other_uk_rules: Scraping and storing bakery owners' contact details is subject to UK GDPR. Suppliers should get clear contract terms because the agent negotiates for the business.

idea.revenue_model: Sales commission (about $10-20k net on a $500k home)
